log.reply:
# Implementation Accelerator Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional)
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, AI Governance Academy
**Source:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. Its headquarters jurisdiction is the Netherlands, and it operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Profile Block records three AI use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. An internal audit finding of June 2026 records no inventory of AI systems.

Dana Whitfield has stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The stated constraints are:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Client's incumbent frameworks are:

- an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS
- an ISO 9001 quality management system
- an internal audit function

ISO/IEC 42001 is the certification target, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed.

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The stated objective places a governance milestone ahead of Q2 2027. An Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) foundation built in five consecutive working days would leave the months between the build and that objective for adoption, review and operation, rather than drafting.

The Accelerator also answers the June 2026 audit finding in its own sequence. The AI system inventory is built on Day 2. The risk register is built from it on Day 3.

Because ISO/IEC 42001 is a target, every artifact will be structured for future conformity work. The aim is readiness. The program does not promise certification, audit results or any assessment outcome.

Each artifact will be designed to attach to the incumbent frameworks rather than stand alone. The specific attachment points within the ISMS and the quality management system are currently `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake. The Profile Block names these frameworks but does not state which registers, processes or records they contain.

At US$25,000, the Accelerator fee sits within the stated approved budget for this fiscal year.

## 3. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to the Client

Two dependencies govern the sequence:

- The inventory is completed before the risk register.
- The charter is completed before the policies.

**Day 1: Governance charter and roles.** The build team drafts the AIMS governance charter. It covers purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence. The working session will set out how AI governance decisions relate to the ISMS, the quality management system and the internal audit function, with attachment points `Unknown` until confirmed. An executive checkpoint closes the day.

**Day 2: AI system inventory and classification.** The team builds the inventory schema and enters the three known use cases as first records. Classification fields will include:

- lifecycle stage
- operating jurisdiction
- personal data involvement under GDPR
- EU data residency status, reflecting the stated customer data constraint
- a provisional EU AI Act category

EU AI Act classification produced during the week is orientation only. Confirm with external counsel.

**Day 3: Risk and impact assessment plus risk register.** Working from the Day 2 inventory, the team runs structured risk and impact assessments and builds the risk register. Seeded risk statements will be grounded in the stated use cases and the June 2026 audit finding. They will be labeled as drafts for Client validation.

For visual inspection, the impact assessment will include a field identifying where works council consultation may be required before any effect on production staff. Whether consultation is required, and when, carries legal effect. Confirm with external counsel.

**Day 4: Core policies and operating procedures.** Working from the adopted Day 1 charter, the team drafts outlines and initial text for:

- acceptable use
- AI lifecycle governance
- vendor and supplier governance
- incident response
- change management

Procedures will be written to attach to the existing management system documentation once attachment points are confirmed.

**Day 5: Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout.** The team builds an evidence index mapping each artifact to the assurance question it answers, structured for future ISO/IEC 42001 conformity work. A prioritized 90-day implementation plan is sequenced against the stated Q2 2027 objective. The week closes with an executive readout. Board-layer framing will draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

The build uses two frameworks:

- the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Three principles shape the work: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 4. Artifacts the Client Owns at Close

At the end of Day 5, the Client owns the following artifacts in editable form. Each carries a status of draft, reviewed or adopted as set during the week.

1. AIMS Governance Charter, including roles, decision rights and meeting cadence
2. AI System Inventory and Classification Schema, populated with the three known use cases
3. AI Risk and Impact Assessment Method
4. AI Risk Register, with seeded risk statements labeled as drafts for Client validation
5. Acceptable Use Policy
6. AI Lifecycle Governance Policy and Procedure
7. Vendor and Supplier Governance Policy
8. AI Incident Response Procedure
9. AI Change Management Procedure
10. Evidence Index mapping each artifact to its assurance question
11. Prioritized 90-Day Implementation Plan with owners
12. Executive Readout

Where each artifact will live in the Client's document system is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

## 5. Team Composition Asked of the Client

We ask the Client to designate a build team that spans the following roles for all five days:

- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- two internal auditors

We also ask the Client to designate executive checkpoint attendees for Days 1 and 5. These attendees are currently `Unknown`.

## 6. Logistics and Price

The Accelerator runs for five consecutive working days as live virtual working sessions with structured build time.

The build is designed to work from governance documentation and system descriptions. It is not designed to require customer data. This is intended to keep the work consistent with the stated EU residency constraint. Session times and start date will be agreed at intake.

The price is US$25,000.

## 7. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. On confirmation, we will schedule a one-hour intake call to agree dates and settle the following questions:

1. Which ISMS and quality management system documents, registers or procedures should each artifact attach to?
2. Where should the artifacts live in the Client's document system?
3. Who will attend the executive checkpoints on Days 1 and 5?
4. Does any part of the Accelerator itself require works council consultation, or does consultation apply only at later implementation stages?
5. Are the chatbot and the visual inspection system supplied by third parties, and if so, which?
6. Which data, if any, will the build team reference during the week, and where is it hosted?

Dana Whitfield, we would welcome a reply confirming your preferred dates for intake.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: Day 4 says 'Working from the adopted Day 1 charter'. I read this as proposed program sequencing, not a Client fact. Another scorer could read it as an assumed status.

Day 4 says procedures 'will be written to attach to the existing management system documentation once attachment points are confirmed'. I read this as conditional proposed work, because the response renders the attachment points Unknown and says the Profile Block does not state the registers or records. A strict scorer could read 'existing management system documentation' as implying incumbent records the Profile Block does not state.

The works council field on the visual inspection impact assessment follows from the stated works council constraint applied to the stated production-line system. Under the v1.14.3 guidance this is not a new Client fact.
The statement that the US$25,000 fee 'sits within the stated approved budget' compares two stated figures. I did not treat it as an inferred relation about who funds what.

Mode A does not call for per-artifact acceptance criteria, so I treated the 'owner, status vocabulary and acceptance criterion' part of item 4 as met on the basis of the Client-owned list and status vocabulary. The page-length requirement is not in the checklist and was not scored.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met. No Client fact beyond the Profile Block is asserted as fact. Unknowns (attachment points, document locations, checkpoint attendees) are rendered Unknown or posed as intake questions, and legal-effect items carry 'Confirm with external counsel.' Incumbent frameworks are named without claiming any register, control or record. The DECISION_TIMELINE is cited as 'A decision is expected by 15 December 2026' with no attribution of whose decision it is. Program name, duration and price are unchanged. The two borderline phrases are conditional or proposed work and not asserted current states, so none of the three fail indicators appears.
